title: 'The old TX-3000s' at a site that also has a TX-5000
description: A tip about 'the old TX-3000s' is given while working on TRN-088 at Jyväskylä Kangas exchange, where the newer TRN-240 (TX-5000) also sits. Tests the vague-word qualifier: the knowledge binds to the instance TRN-088 only, a class built from 'old' is flagged as wider than stated (or rejected by the critic), and the site is where it was seen, not scope.
subject: Kangas exchange, TRN-088 power cycle

messages.text: at Kangas exchange now, power cycled TRN-088 after the fan alarm. the OSPF neighbour did not come back 😕
the old TX-3000s do that after a power cycle, they need a manual 'clear ospf neighbor' on the uplink port
right. wait 5 min after boot, then clear the neighbour. before that it just flaps
ok did it on TRN-088, neighbour is up. should I do the same on TRN-240 next to it?
no, that one is a TX-5000, different firmware, it comes up on its own

items.summary: After a power cycle TRN-088 (an older TX-3000) does not restore its OSPF neighbour by itself: wait 5 minutes after boot, then run 'clear ospf neighbor' on the uplink port. The neighbouring TX-5000 TRN-240 is not affected.
items.action: Wait 5 minutes after boot, then run 'clear ospf neighbor' on the uplink port.
avoid: expect the OSPF neighbour to come back on its own after a power cycle
items.evidence: seq 3-4: 'the old TX-3000s do that after a power cycle' / 'wait 5 min after boot, then clear the neighbour'
items.evidence_quote: the old TX-3000s do that after a power cycle, they need a manual 'clear ospf neighbor' on the uplink port
